## US-Venezuela Tensions Escalate in December 2025 Amid Sanctions and Military Pressure

In the latter half of December 2025, relations between the United States and Venezuela were marked by a significant escalation of American pressure, including new sanctions and a naval blockade that severely impacted Venezuela's oil exports. This period of heightened tension immediately preceded a U.S. military strike in early January 2026 that resulted in the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. [pbs.org](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHhLwFHJ8XgAiH8hMCxndn2_omHYnYwwZVQAbqc1GXtrEvpGxAE0ZdU7SiR5jLZHHJ6y1im8wa0v2kDqYgeutDXtqsU1MQvqBduhSwYWNzo1PrZxRQLuhOIp5ppkl2iyOmnDyPZ4hoElExrQ9TpTlex-anE1SYX1yvxJp9xNRzPTMczHBNpXySvbtfbn9ZckTcFoU6zhjfP8mLmPYiU) [un.org](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHk2b3bfozYf5ciQTdhXDWwCFSVN9-cv5RrjfQK7Lpfcc9vQBHLjGliIKIeZdhpRLGAjYYgd2SU9P9L11pM8W8ukrdxuMn1TVCYbRgdgmKnni5sY-G5ooFJQuB5XzW00pK68a3cj48=)

Throughout December 2025, the U.S. intensified its sanctions campaign against the Maduro regime. [debuglies.com](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGGQp6hzcKxWjv63TQuAJjxOtBMLlH2vqqCtcRLmjTMkFCmfdHUvGs9xYNBHj-lNfZIOZmiuAfKrX6VnnSIk-zK4iwSkKzrXKXH8AL3M0_vwyP2cTTCiRpHLiwKxLKAK1oioJTSd-0JSzLe7UH1GDcCTMej0Qfa0VBnbEJ2oB7tn1TGAT44lE2N3fq4laQxGmXdnyQ4FndnHUaqtWoIQ94Ai3fMgocqdt4Rl80jf6ogWhAXf8uEZiuJzFSloji0ScIKHjFmQ-XSvkjEcZo7r6fDkX5faoXJwQ310ZIP5aFhu0gDaJ4rMGV3lT4z5u1hWEFQ) The Treasury Department targeted officials, their families, and multiple companies and oil tankers for their role in Venezuela's oil sector, which Washington asserted was fueling an "illegitimate narco-terrorist regime." [debuglies.com](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGGQp6hzcKxWjv63TQuAJjxOtBMLlH2vqqCtcRLmjTMkFCmfdHUvGs9xYNBHj-lNfZIOZmiuAfKrX6VnnSIk-zK4iwSkKzrXKXH8AL3M0_vwyP2cTTCiRpHLiwKxLKAK1oioJTSd-0JSzLe7UH1GDcCTMej0Qfa0VBnbEJ2oB7tn1TGAT44lE2N3fq4laQxGmXdnyQ4FndnHUaqtWoIQ94Ai3fMgocqdt4Rl80jf6ogWhAXf8uEZiuJzFSloji0ScIKHjFmQ-XSvkjEcZo7r6fDkX5faoXJwQ310ZIP5aFhu0gDaJ4rMGV3lT4z5u1hWEFQ) [treasury.gov](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGkGO5svfgDpbxpDEHks78dO198HKZAIU5kFxZWyANdQ4Mp0KD4SBKdBXcW2JYsk03gqXDhzdCNfkEMNUKduPm5LRwaas4OPQum--Qs8ryRLdpHRuh-WhnuQ7xfshn2NCz3HAvHBdEPBIBAiAs5Sw==) [cbsnews.com](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFgcfSdnjXOL9ZtdWe2KANvX-Ylhovsu9aDfdPuHChX_akMYoPRer1VNkamZpCRCqHOEvW3_hLoLYfdbO3IjxqRtFXfDpS6lQk5MPWN9VR6Qfar-C-bnx4ksMQ_d21Y7hCJLwQssAc3IoJQJ4tNAZp3bslzMsKVESUbsNiWvQq3C_mYLkw=) These actions complemented sanctions imposed on December 11 and December 19 against officials and vessels linked to the state-run oil company, PDVSA. [treasury.gov](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGkGO5svfgDpbxpDEHks78dO198HKZAIU5kFxZWyANdQ4Mp0KD4SBKdBXcW2JYsk03gqXDhzdCNfkEMNUKduPm5LRwaas4OPQum--Qs8ryRLdpHRuh-WhnuQ7xfshn2NCz3HAvHBdEPBIBAiAs5Sw==)

The most significant development during this month was the severe disruption of Venezuela's oil industry due to U.S. pressure. [argaam.com](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGbNkiGrjQuaSfO4OF47DA8NTyxE6RUgBWQF9IAEVUSFmvDt00pr4MNzfSKqp13AByAosez44RYkeb9S9J6LaCUQ_pMTbJMyMPy9nv1mXPeQxK5HVG_5EpeLAXt3vjClBEXj_2Nlu--mMF6DonuBfR4vQwuYw==) An American naval blockade, part of "Operation Southern Spear," created a high risk of seizure for tankers, particularly those in the "shadow fleet" used to transport sanctioned oil to Asia. [vortexa.com](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQENadrSBuHYzbHuol_-Xix8-O3AnCoHYZhUfMutbc97kMlttrX2Jf36M43DIg5RppxY-OdCtjZtIFsiWydmvSlI6GOV15QrYLug0E0JndQ9EwzVdz4oIi-jC4ok8PwrNbhY5_kRqUwkn4THZXlPM8l7CCDBkmZsWYy1) This led to a 36% drop in Venezuela's seaborne crude exports for December, with volumes falling to just under 600,000 barrels per day. [vortexa.com](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQENadrSBuHYzbHuol_-Xix8-O3AnCoHYZhUfMutbc97kMlttrX2Jf36M43DIg5RppxY-OdCtjZtIFsiWydmvSlI6GOV15QrYLug0E0JndQ9EwzVdz4oIi-jC4ok8PwrNbhY5_kRqUwkn4THZXlPM8l7CCDBkmZsWYy1) The logistical bottleneck forced at least 15 million barrels of crude into floating storage as tanker operators delayed departures or made mid-voyage U-turns to avoid seizure. [vortexa.com](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQENadrSBuHYzbHuol_-Xix8-O3AnCoHYZhUfMutbc97kMlttrX2Jf36M43DIg5RppxY-OdCtjZtIFsiWydmvSlI6GOV15QrYLug0E0JndQ9EwzVdz4oIi-jC4ok8PwrNbhY5_kRqUwkn4THZXlPM8l7CCDBkmZsWYy1) [offshore-technology.com](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFzTYi-9ndEIHWlVTBdBBoJbC3vK0UwJQpLnABcV2ZepIAIILpDAWUX0cUr9O3xEv_RZ1iBTTb_BguDq7T-kVAkzzTjulj7kz-h7o1sa15aFHMB_38rwx2scCCwzZ2HwSnQ4CoudFPURIQ_59dxkzHCinusi1hdVJ5uol_QJqFW5sPLk5Y1VQ==) By the end of the month, the state oil company PDVSA was reportedly slowing deliveries and considering production cuts as its onshore storage capacity neared its limits. [offshore-technology.com](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFzTYi-9ndEIHWlVTBdBBoJbC3vK0UwJQpLnABcV2ZepIAIILpDAWUX0cUr9O3xEv_RZ1iBTTb_BguDq7T-kVAkzzTjulj7kz-h7o1sa15aFHMB_38rwx2scCCwzZ2HwSnQ4CoudFPURIQ_59dxkzHCinusi1hdVJ5uol_QJqFW5sPLk5Y1VQ==)

While the U.S. campaign crippled much of Venezuela's exports, licensed shipments by the U.S. company Chevron remained resilient, accounting for about 100,000 barrels per day. [vortexa.com](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQENadrSBuHYzbHuol_-Xix8-O3AnCoHYZhUfMutbc97kMlttrX2Jf36M43DIg5RppxY-OdCtjZtIFsiWydmvSlI6GOV15QrYLug0E0JndQ9EwzVdz4oIi-jC4ok8PwrNbhY5_kRqUwkn4THZXlPM8l7CCDBkmZsWYy1)

The UN's top human rights official warned on December 16, 2025, that repression was tightening its grip in Venezuela amid shrinking accountability. [un.org](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHk2b3bfozYf5ciQTdhXDWwCFSVN9-cv5RrjfQK7Lpfcc9vQBHLjGliIKIeZdhpRLGAjYYgd2SU9P9L11pM8W8ukrdxuMn1TVCYbRgdgmKnni5sY-G5ooFJQuB5XzW00pK68a3cj48=) By December 23, the escalating U.S. military operations in the Southern Caribbean prompted warnings at the UN Security Council about violations of sovereignty and calls for de-escalation. [un.org](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHk2b3bfozYf5ciQTdhXDWwCFSVN9-cv5RrjfQK7Lpfcc9vQBHLjGliIKIeZdhpRLGAjYYgd2SU9P9L11pM8W8ukrdxuMn1TVCYbRgdgmKnni5sY-G5ooFJQuB5XzW00pK68a3cj48=) These events set the stage for direct U.S. military action in the following weeks.

grounding_supports.segment_text: This period of heightened tension immediately preceded a U.S. military strike in early January 2026 that resulted in the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.
Throughout December 2025, the U.S. intensified its sanctions campaign against the Maduro regime.

The Treasury Department targeted officials, their families, and multiple companies and oil tankers for their role in Venezuela's oil sector, which Washington asserted was fueling an "illegitimate narco-terrorist regime."
These actions complemented sanctions imposed on December 11 and December 19 against officials and vessels linked to the state-run oil company, PDVSA.
The most significant development during this month was the severe disruption of Venezuela's oil industry due to U.S. pressure.
An American naval blockade, part of "Operation Southern Spear," created a high risk of seizure for tankers, particularly those in the "shadow fleet" used to transport sanctioned oil to Asia.
This led to a 36% drop in Venezuela's seaborne crude exports for December, with volumes falling to just under 600,000 barrels per day.
The logistical bottleneck forced at least 15 million barrels of crude into floating storage as tanker operators delayed departures or made mid-voyage U-turns to avoid seizure.
By the end of the month, the state oil company PDVSA was reportedly slowing deliveries and considering production cuts as its onshore storage capacity neared its limits.
While the U.S. campaign crippled much of Venezuela's exports, licensed shipments by the U.S. company Chevron remained resilient, accounting for about 100,000 barrels per day.
The UN's top human rights official warned on December 16, 2025, that repression was tightening its grip in Venezuela amid shrinking accountability.
By December 23, the escalating U.S. military operations in the Southern Caribbean prompted warnings at the UN Security Council about violations of sovereignty and calls for de-escalation.
